Bhagavad Gita, Chapter 3, Verse 13

“The good, who eat what remains after sacrifice, are freed from all faults. But the wicked, who cook only for themselves, eat their own wrong.”

The distinction is not what is eaten but what came first. Food received as a remainder nourishes; the very same food taken as entitlement becomes consuming one's own harm.
